Sure they can. Just because it's a trademark doesn't mean you're suddenly not allowed to use it in regular speech. Trademarks aren't like patents where the owner of a patent can outright forbid you use in every circumstance. All they can do is forbid you from using it to promote or identify a product or service. The biggest concern is "let's play" videos, but you can't call trademark infringement on basic communication. If I title my video "Let's play Minecraft" and then I proceed to create a video of me playing Minecraft, there's no possible way Sony could prevent me from using that title. The case would never hold up in court because it's not being used as a brand - it's just describing content.

If I were to create a company around creating videos and then I used "Let's play" with my logo as a means to identify my product, then Sony would have a case.

There are lots of examples of companies registering trademarks for common speech. Some of the most well known would be Nike (Just do it) and McDonalds (I'm lovin' it), Apple (think different), Budweisser (Wassup?!), Cadilac (Break through), Coors (The silver bullet) - many, many other examples could be found.

All we're seeing here is a loud, mostly ignorant group screaming about something they clearly do not understand.

There's rules to making something so common a phrase. If it would create confusion to trademark it (which "let's play!" could easily do, in my opinion) it will be shot down. I guess they could try to trademark it, but what I'm trying to get at here is, ultimately, the attempt to copyright it will probably fail.
